quotes.text: The organizations that are winning with AI right now aren't the ones with the best models. They are the ones with the best connectivity layer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes AI success as an integration architecture problem rather than a model problem.

quotes.text: MCP doesn't replace Microsoft Graph. It doesn't replace your REST APIs. It doesn't replace your custom connectors. It sits above them. MCP is the translation layer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly positions MCP relative to existing Microsoft integration options.

quotes.text: A2A isn't a competitor to MCP. It solves a different problem. MCP connects agents to tools. A2A connects agents to other agents. You need both.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise distinction between the two agent protocols architects need.

quotes.text: The agent should reason. It should decide which tools to invoke. It should synthesize results. But it should not implement business rules. Business rules belong in the MCP server where they can be versioned, tested and reused across multiple agents.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable design rule that avoids the most common MCP anti-pattern.

quotes.text: MCP isn't just a protocol. It's an architectural pattern. It changes how your agents connect to systems. It changes how your systems expose capabilities. It changes how your security team thinks about identity.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes why MCP must be treated as architecture, not just integration.

takeaways: MCP sits above Microsoft Graph, REST APIs and connectors as a standard discovery and capability layer, so one MCP server can serve every agent in the organization.
Use STDIO only for local development and streamable HTTP behind Azure API Management with Entra authentication for production; SSE is deprecated.
Combine MCP for tools with A2A for agent collaboration, and secure every agent with Entra Agent ID, Conditional Access and Agent 365 from day one.
hook: Most AI pilots stall not because the model is weak but because agents cannot reach the systems that hold the data. This episode gives Microsoft architects a practical guide to the Model Context Protocol, from the wire protocol and C# SDK to Azure deployment, Copilot Studio, Work IQ, A2A and agent identity, ending with a 90-day roadmap to production.
